beginner.about: Learn the basics of the game in this introductory mode designed for new players.
rules: Gain resources by rolling the dice
Trade with the bank or with your opponents for missing resources
Build roads, settlements, and cities to expand your empire

faq.question: What is Beginner Mode?
faq.answer: Beginner Mode is a simplified version of the game designed to help new players learn the basic mechanics in less than 5 minutes.

faq.question: Do I need to know the rules before playing?
faq.answer: No! Beginner Mode is perfect for first-time players. The game guides you through the basics and uses simplified rules to help you learn as you play.

faq.question: Can I play with other players?
faq.answer: Beginner Mode is a single-player experience against bots, so you can learn at your own pace without pressure.

easy.about: Practice against easy AI opponents and learn basic game mechanics.
rules: Play against 3 easy bots
Practice game mechanics and basic strategies
Place two initial settlements and roads
Roll the dice to gather resources and expand your empire
First to 10 Victory Points wins. Discard Limit is 7 resource cards

faq.question: How difficult are the Easy bots?
faq.answer: Easy bots make simple strategic decisions and are great for practicing basic game mechanics. They provide a relaxed gaming experience perfect for learning.

faq.question: Can I pause the game?
faq.answer: Yes! Since you're playing against bots, you can take your time with each move. The game will wait for you.

faq.question: Do bots trade fairly?
faq.answer: Easy bots will accept reasonable trades, making it easier to learn the trading system and complete your objectives.

medium.about: Test your skills against more challenging AI opponents.
rules: Face 3 medium difficulty bots
Improve your trading and building strategies
Place two initial settlements and roads
Roll the dice to gather resources and expand your empire
First to 10 Victory Points wins. Discard Limit is 7 resource cards

faq.question: How difficult are Medium bots?
faq.answer: Medium bots use more advanced strategies and are better at blocking opponents. They provide a moderate challenge for players looking to improve their skills.

faq.question: Will bots accept trades?
faq.answer: Medium bots are more selective with trades and will only accept offers that benefit them, similar to human players.

faq.question: Is this good practice for online play?
faq.answer: Yes! Medium bots provide good preparation for playing against real players by using more strategic decision-making.

hard.about: Face the toughest AI opponents and master advanced strategies.
rules: Challenge yourself against 3 hard bots
Master advanced tactics and resource management
Place two initial settlements and roads
Roll the dice to gather resources and expand your empire
First to 10 Victory Points wins. Discard Limit is 7 resource cards

faq.question: How challenging are Hard bots?
faq.answer: Hard bots use advanced strategies, optimal placement, and aggressive blocking tactics. They provide a serious challenge even for experienced players.

faq.question: Do Hard bots trade?
faq.answer: Hard bots rarely trade and will only accept trades that significantly benefit them. They prioritize winning over cooperation.

faq.question: What strategies do Hard bots use?
faq.answer: Hard bots use advanced tactics like being very selective with trades, and using strategic robber positioning to gain maximum advantage.

casual1v1.about: Fast-paced 1v1 matches against real players. Quick games with strategic depth.
rules: Quick 1v1 matches in the classic base game board
Only players with 3 or more points can be blocked by the robber (Friendly Robber mechanic)
First to 15 Victory Points wins. Discard Limit is 9 resource cards

faq.question: How is 1v1 different from 4-player?
faq.answer: 1v1 features faster gameplay, and requires 15 Victory Points to win instead of the standard amount. Also, the Discard Limit is 9 cards in hand.

faq.question: How long does a 1v1 match take?
faq.answer: Most 1v1 matches take around 10 minutes, making it perfect for quick games when you don't have time for a full 4P match.

faq.question: Is there a ranked version?
faq.answer: Yes! You can play Ranked 1v1 to compete for rating and climb the leaderboards with the same fast-paced format.

casual4Player.about: Classic 4-player matches with real opponents. Experience the full depth of Catan strategy.
rules: Classic 4-player Catan experience
Trade, build, and strategize with 3 other players
First to 10 Victory Points wins. Discard Limit is 7 resource cards

faq.question: How many players are in a match?
faq.answer: 4-player matches include you and 3 other players, providing the classic Catan experience with full player interaction and trading.

faq.question: Can I play with friends?
faq.answer: Yes! You can create a custom room and invite friends, or play in matchmaking to be paired with players of similar skill level.

faq.question: How long does a game take?
faq.answer: Most 4-player games take around 30 minutes, though this can vary based on player decisions and game complexity.

shuffle.about: Play a new game mode every week!
rules: You'll have to figure out on your own, as each Shuffle mode is completely unique 😉.

faq.question: What is Shuffle mode?
faq.answer: Shuffle changes every week, bringing new combinations of game modes, maps, and player counts.

faq.question: When does the queue change?
faq.answer: Once a week, usually on Wednesdays.

faq.question: How often can I play?
faq.answer: Everyone gets 5 free plays. Afterwards 1 free play every day. Become a Member for unlimited access!

faq.question: Are all game modes and maps eligible?
faq.answer: Yes!

faq.question: Which player counts are eligible?
faq.answer: Shuffle includes 2, 4, 6, and 8 player games.

ranked1v1.about: Compete in Ranked 1v1 matches to climb the leaderboard and improve your rating.
rules: Compete for rating and climb the ranked leaderboard
Matched with players of similar skill level
First to 15 Victory Points wins. Discard Limit is 9 resource cards

faq.question: How does ranked rating work?
faq.answer: You gain or lose rating based on match results. Winning increases your rating, and losing decreases it. The system matches you with players of similar skill level.

faq.question: What are placement matches?
faq.answer: Your first ranked matches of each season help determine your starting rating. Play your best, as these matches have a large impact on your initial ranking. Placement games are reseted with every new season.

faq.question: Is rating reset after a season ends?
faq.answer: Yes, there is a soft reset of your rating. However, your performance on previous seasons is considered and will impact your rating gains/losses.

ranked4P.about: Test your skills in competitive 4-player ranked matches. Earn your rating and climb the ranks.
rules: Compete in ranked 4-player matches for rating
Strategic gameplay with competitive players
Complete placement matches to establish your rating
First to 10 Victory Points wins. Discard Limit is 7 resource cards

faq.question: How does ranked rating work?
faq.answer: You gain or lose rating based on match results. Winning increases your rating, and losing decreases it. The system matches you with players of similar skill level.

faq.question: What are placement matches?
faq.answer: Your first ranked matches of each season help determine your starting rating. Play your best, as these matches have a large impact on your initial ranking. Placement games are reseted with every new season.

faq.question: Is rating reset after a season ends?
faq.answer: Yes, there is a soft reset of your rating. However, your performance on previous seasons is considered and will impact your rating gains/losses.

faq.answer: Yes! Colonist Rush adds urgency to the base game. We recommend mastering standard 4P Catan before trying this mode. You can also practice Colonist Rush against Bots.

citiesAndKnights.about: Experience the Cities & Knights expansion, with additional mechanics, greater strategic depth, and increased complexity.
rules: Build cities to obtain Commodities, used to purchase city improvements
The more city improvements you get, the more Progress Cards you'll obtain

formats.question: 1. What game formats are allowed? (1v1, 3P, 4P..)
formats.answer: All game formats are allowed. You are free to run your tournament however you see fit with your audience.

ruleset.question: 2. Do you have a default tournament ruleset I can use?

minimumPlayers.question: 3. What happens if I get less than 16 players joining my qualifier?
minimumPlayers.answer: Reach out to nearby communities to explore co-hosting. We can help connect you with other applicants in your area. If not possible, run your qualifier as planned. Your winner will attend a pre-Championship knockout round.

eligibility.question: 4. Who is eligible to play in the Colonist Championship 2026?
eligibility.answer: Anyone above age 13 that has logged into Colonist and owns an account.

entryFees.question: 5. Can I charge entry fees?
entryFees.answer: Yes, you're free to host however fits your audience. However, the fees are charged only by the host and Colonist does not ask for any participation fee for the Championship.

public.question: 6. Do qualifiers have to be public?
public.answer: Not necessarily, you can set your own limits.

attendance.question: 7. What if a player can't attend the Championship games?
attendance.answer: You can submit the next-in-line from your qualifier.

rewards.question: 8. How are rewards delivered?
rewards.answer: For the qualifier finalists, we'll send the host Membership links for the finalists to redeem. For Championship finalists, Colonist will cover the shipping and delivery.

hostingSupport.question: 9. I have a large online community but don't have the resources to hold an online tournament. Will Colonist help me host a tournament?

resources.question: 10. Will Colonist provide venues, cash prizes, and staff?
resources.answer: No. You can reach out to other companies for local sponsorship. Before finalizing, contact us at tournament@colonist.io. We will do our best to support you!

ccpa.header: CCPA Privacy Rights (Do Not Sell My Personal Information)
ccpa.underTheCcpa: Under the CCPA, among other rights, California consumers have the right to:
ccpa.requestDisclose: Request that a business that collects a consumer's personal data disclose the categories and specific pieces of personal data that a business has collected about consumers.
ccpa.requestDelete: Request that a business delete any personal data about the consumer that a business has collected.
ccpa.requestNotSell: Request that a business that sells a consumer's personal data, not sell the consumer's personal data.
ccpa.ifYouMakeARequest: If you make a request, we have one month to respond to you. If you would like to exercise any of these rights, please contact us.

gdpr.fullyAware: We would like to make sure you are fully aware of all of your data protection rights. Every user is entitled to the following:
gdpr.rightToAccess: The right to access – You have the right to request copies of your personal data. We may charge you a small fee for this service.
gdpr.rightToRectification: The right to rectification – You have the right to request that we correct any information you believe is inaccurate. You also have the right to request that we complete the information you believe is incomplete.
gdpr.rightToErasure: The right to erasure – You have the right to request that we erase your personal data, under certain conditions. To delete your account, go to colonist.io/profile, click on Account in the side panel, and click the Delete button. If you are a Member, you need to manually cancel your Membership and wait until it expeires before deleting your account.
gdpr.rightToRestrict: The right to restrict processing – You have the right to request that we restrict the processing of your personal data, under certain conditions.
gdpr.rightToObject: The right to object to processing – You have the right to object to our processing of your personal data, under certain conditions.
gdpr.rightToPortability: The right to data portability – You have the right to request that we transfer the data that we have collected to another organization, or directly to you, under certain conditions.

children.addingProtection: Another part of our priority is adding protection for children while using the internet. We encourage parents and guardians to observe, participate in, and/or monitor and guide their online activity.
children.doesNotKnowingly: Colonist does not knowingly collect any Personal Identifiable Information from children under the age of 13. If you think that your child provided this kind of information on our website, we strongly encourage you to contact us immediately and we will do our best efforts to promptly remove such information from our records.

instructions: Click on Safari located in the menu bar of your browser and select Preferences

options on the left.

Return to the video loaded in Safari, click Continue watching

instructions: Click the gear icon to open Settings.
Select the Manage Add-ons option on the drop-down list.
Click the Toolbars and Extensions link in the left navigation pane.
Right-click the AdBlock add-on name in the list, then click the Disable button.
Click the Disable button in the confirmation window to disable the Adblock add-on.
Refresh this page and you're all good to go.

others.mightBeFollowingReasons: Your ads might be blocked for the following reasons.

reasons.programs: Computer/mobile device programs -> Check to see if you installed any other adblock programs to your device. Some people use Kaspersky.
reasons.network: Wifi, router, firewall, VPN -> Talk with your wifi setup to see if it has adblock installed.
reasons.isp: ISP -> Talk with your ISP to see if they're blocking your ads.
reasons.country: Country -> We haven't seen this case but we wouldn't be surprised.

colonistRush.title: $t(strings:colonistCommon.gameModes.colonistRush.title)
colonistRush.description: Complete rules for the Colonist Rush game mode on Colonist, the free online Settlers of Catan alternative. How to play without turns and more!

section1.title: 1. No Turns
section1.desc2: All players can build, buy development cards, and trade at any time, in parallel.

section2.title: 2. Automatic Dice Rolls
section2.desc1: Dice roll automatically at regular intervals (configured in room settings).
section2.desc2: When dice roll, resources are distributed to all players simultaneously.

section3.title: 3. Rolling a 7
section3.desc1: On each 7 roll, players take turns to move the robber.
section3.desc2: While a player is moving the robber, others can still build, buy development cards, and trade. So move fast!
section3.desc3: There is always a robber icon next to the player who will move the robber next.

section4.title: 4. Discarding Cards
section4.desc1: Default card discard limit is 9 cards. If players must discard cards after a 7 roll:
section4.list1: Only the players who need to discard can act.
section4.list2: All other players are temporarily locked.
section4.list3: The game resumes only after all required discards are completed.

section5.title: 5. Vote to Roll Immediately
section5.desc1: Players can vote to roll the dice early instead of waiting for the timer.
section5.desc2: If all active players vote, the dice roll immediately.
section5.desc3: This keeps the game fast when everyone is ready.

bg.title: $t(strings:leaderboardPage.gameModes.baseGame)
bg.description: Complete rules for the Base Game on Colonist, the free online Settlers of Catan alternative. How to play Dev Cards and roads, what to do when 7 rolls, and more!

section1.title: 1. How to win
section1.firstPlayerTo10VP: The first player that gets to 10 Points is the winner. Get points by doing the following:
section1.upgradeSettlementToCity: Upgrade a settlement to a city
section1.buyVPDevelopmentCard: Buy Development Cards for a chance to get a +1 Point Card
section1.getLongestRoad: Get the Longest Road. A minimum of 5 consecutive roads is required to get this achievement
section1.getLargestArmy: Get the Largest Army. Playing a minimum of 3 Knight Development Cards is required to get this achievement
section1.stealingAchievements: Other players can steal Longest Road or Largest Army if they have more roads or played knights!

section2.title: 2. Initial placements
section2.placeOneSettlement: Placement: Players will take turns to place two settlements {{- settlementIcon}} and two roads {{- roadIcon}}, one coming from each settlement.
section2.collectingResources: Collecting resources: You will get a resource from each of the tiles surrounding your 2nd settlement {{- settlementIcon}}
section2.placeSettlementsTwoRoadsApart: All settlements must be at least two roads apart

section3.title: 3. Dice rolls
section3.afterInitialPlacements: After the initial placements, every player takes turns rolling the dice at the start of their turn. Each dice roll determines what resources are distributed: every time the dice rolls, the resources with that number in the board will be distributed amongst the players with settlements or cities around those tiles.
section3.diceRollProbability: Each dice roll has a different probability of rolling, represented with dots below the numbers. 7 is the number most likely to roll, followed by 6 and 8.

section4.title: 4. Collecting resources
section4.ofEachResource: There are 19 of each resource card

section5.title: 5. Robber & discards
section5.when7Rolled: Whenever a 7 is rolled the following happens:
section5.allPlayersOverDiscardLimit: Players holding 8 or more cards must discard half of them to the bank (rounded down in case of an odd number)
section5.blockAndSteal: Block and steal cards with the Robber
section5.moveRobber: The player who rolled a 7 shall move the Robber to block a resource from future rolls. They also steal one resource from a player on that tile.

section6.title: 6. Building & buying costs
section6.buildLimit: Each player can build a maximum of 15 roads, 5 settlements and 4 cities.

section7.title: 7. Development Cards
section7.developmentCardExplanation: Development Cards have special abilities. There are 25 total in the deck and they can be played before the dice is rolled.
section7.devCardKnight: Move the Robber to another tile and steal one random resource from a player on that tile
section7.devCardYearOfPlenty: Select 2 resources of your choice from the bank
section7.devCardMonopoly: Steal all resources of one type from all other players
section7.devCardVictoryPoint: Player secretly gets awarded 1 Point. +1 Point cards are revealed once you reach 10 points.
section7.oneDevCardPerTurn: You can only play 1 Development Card per turn. You may not play a Development Card on the same turn that you bought it.

section8.title: 8. Trading
section8.tradeDescription: You can trade with other players, or with the bank.
section8.tradeWithBank: You can trade with the bank. Trade 4 resources of the same type in return for 1 resource of your choosing.
section8.tradeWith3to1: Build a settlement on a 3:1 port to trade any 3 resources of the same type for 1 resource of your choosing.
section8.tradeWith2to1: Build a settlement on a 2:1 port to trade 2 resources of the port type for any 1 resource of your choosing.
section8.tradeWithPlayers: You can trade any number or combination of resources with other players for any combination or number of resources in return (but you can't trade the same type of resource).

section9.title: 9. FAQ
section9.Q1: ● Do I keep Longest Road or Largest Army after someone builds the same amount of roads, or plays the same amount of knights?
section9.A1: Yes, you only lose Longest Road or Largest Army when someone has more roads or knights than you. So you keep the bonus if someone has the same amount.

56p.title: 5-6 / 7-8 Players
56p.description: Complete rules for the 5-6 & 7-8 Player Expansions on Colonist, the free online Settlers of Catan alternative. How to use the Special Build Phase and more!

section1.title: 1. Special Build Phase
section1.clickRedFlag: Click the red flag button to access a Special Build Phase after each of the other players' regular turn.
section1.specialBuildPhaseYouCan:
You can ✅

Build roads, settlements, cities, or buy a Development Card
section1.specialBuildPhaseYouCant:
You cannot ❌

1. Make trades
2. Use a Development Card
3. Win during the Special Build Phase. You must wait until it becomes your turn again

section2.title: 2. Additional resources
section2.numberOfResourceCards: Total number of each resource card

section3.title: 3. Cities & Knights 5-6 Player
section3.referToCitiesAndKnights: Refer to $t(strings:rulebook.56p.section3.citiesAndKnightsRules) for gameplay during the build phase, there are also actions that can be taken on Knights.
section3.citiesAndKnightsYouCant:
You cannot ❌

Displace an opponent's Knight
Use the Robber

section4.title: 4. FAQ
section4.Q1: ● May I play a Development Card I bought in Special Build Phase, right before my regular turn?
section4.A1: Yes, you are allowed to play that Development Card in your turn. The Special Build Phase right before your turn is not part of your regular turn.
section4.Q2: ●  May I perform a Knight action with a Knight I activated in Special Build Phase right before my turn?
section4.A2: Yes, you are allowed to use that Knight in that turn. The Special Build Phase right before your turn is not part of your regular turn.

sf.title: $t(strings:colonistCommon.gameModes.seafarers4P.title)
sf.description: Complete rules for Seafarers Expansion on Colonist, the free online Settlers of Catan alternative. How to play with ships, Barbarian Ships, gold/fog tiles, and more!

section1.title: 1. New Game Pieces
section1.shipsAllowYouToTravel: Ships allow you to travel across sea tiles to discover new islands
section1.pirateShipsBlockPlayers: Pirate Ship blocks player ships from being placed or moved, and also steals a resource
section1.seaHexes: Sea hexes are what you build ships on
section1.goldHexes: Gold tiles give you a resource of your choice when their number is rolled

section2.title: 2. Ships
section2.buildShips: Build ships to discover new islands & resources to build settlements on.
section2.openAndClosedRoutes:
Open routes - Once per turn, you may move a ship that is not connecting settlements.
Closed routes - Ships that are connecting settlements cannot be moved.
section2.shipsMustConnect: Ships must start from & connect to a settlement. They cannot start from a road.

section3.title: 3. Longest Trade Route
section3.longestTradeRouteReplaces:
Longest Trade Route replaces Longest Road for 2 Points.
Build a minimum of 5 roads, ships, or a combination of both to get the Longest Trade Route.

section4.title: 4. Robber and Pirate Ship
section4.when7Rolls: Whenever a 7 rolls, the player can choose to move either the Robber or the Pirate Ship.
section4.canOnlyBePlacedOnSeaHex: Can only be placed on a sea tile
section4.allowPlayerToSteal: Allows players to steal from opponents with ships on that tile
section4.blockPlayersFromBuilding: Blocks players from building new ships on that tile
section4.blockPlayersFromMoving: Blocks players from moving ships to and from that tile

section5.title: 5. Discovering New Islands
section5.additional2VP: Get an additional 2 {{- trophyIcon}} Points for the first settlement you build on a new island in the following Scenarios: New Shores, Four Islands, Though The Desert (building across the desert will also grant 2 additional VPs).
section5.someMapsMight: Some maps might have a {{- fogTile}} Fog tile which will uncover a random resource or sea tile. You will get a free resource every time you reveal a fog tile.

section7.title: 7. Points to Win
section7.firstPersonTo13VP:
The first person to get to 13 {{- trophyIcon}} Points is the winner (this might change depending on the Scenario).
Get points by doing the following:
section7.longestTradeRoute: Have the Longest Trade Route (5 roads/ships minimum)
section7.buildSettlementOnIsland: Build a settlement on an island

section8.title: 8. FAQ
section8.Q1: ● Can I build roads, settlements, and cities next to the Pirate Ship?
section8.A1: Yes, the Pirate only blocks ships from being placed or moved.

ck.title: $t(strings:homePage.ranked.citiesAndKnights)
ck.description: Complete rules for the Cities & Knights Expansion on Colonist, the free online Settlers of Catan alternative. How to play with knights, barbarians, and more!

section2.title: 2. Initial Placements
section2.placeSettlementAndCity: On your second initial placement, place a {{- cityIcon}} city instead of a {{- settlementIcon}} settlement.

section3.title: 3. Types of Dice
section3.thereAre3TypesOfDice: There are 3 types of dice: regular, red, and event dice.
section3.redDiceDescription: The red die determines if players earn a Progress Card based on the players’ City Improvement levels. For detailed information about Progress Card distribution and its relation with the red die, click here.
section3.eventDiceDescription: The Event die has 3 Barbarian Ships, and 3 Castles. Each Castle represents a Progress Card type.
section3.barbarianShip:
Barbarian Ship - A ship on the Event die means the Barbarian Ship moves forward 1 space on the barbarian tracker
Castle - Distributes Progress Cards based on the castle’s color, the value of the Red die, and the player’s City Improvement levels.

section4.title: 4. Collecting Commodities
section4.cityProduction: Cities placed on Wool, Lumber, or Ore produce 1 resource & 1 commodity.
section4.importantToKnow: Important things to know about commodities:
section4.countTowardsDiscardLimit: Commodities count towards Robber discard limit
section4.canBeTraded: Commodities can be traded like any other resource
section4.mustHaveCity: Commodities can only be used to buy City Improvements as long as you have at least 1 city on the board

section5.title: 5. Barbarians
section5.barbariansDescription:
When a Barbarian Ship is rolled on the Event die, barbarians move one space forward on the track. Barbarian strength is equal to the sum of all cities on the board.

{{- cityRedIcon}} + {{- cityGreenIcon}} + {{- cityGoldIcon}} = 3 Barbarian strength

section6.title: 6. Knights
section6.canBePlacedAnywhere: Can be placed anywhere at the end of or in between roads
section6.canBreakAnotherRoad: Can break another player’s road length when placed in between their roads
section6.youCannotPlace:
You CAN place a knight & activate it on the same turn.
You CANNOT place a knight, activate a knight, and take a knight action.
section6.knightLimit: Each player can have 2 Basic knights, 2 Strong knights, and 2 Mighty knights.
section6.upgradingKnightsCost: Upgrading a knight costs 1 Wool and 1 Ore.
section6.upgradingKnightsRules:
Upgraded knights will remain active or inactive.
You CAN place a level 1 knight & upgrade it on the same turn.
You CANNOT upgrade a knight twice on the same turn.
You can ONLY upgrade to level 3 knights after you reach the third level in Politic City Improvements (Fortress). However, you can obtain a level 3 knight without having Fortress, by using a Deserter card on another player who has a level 3 knight.
section6.knightActions: Knight actions (these will deactivate your knight):
section6.moveKnight: Moving the knight - move a knight to any available spot in the same road network.
section6.displacingKnight: Displacing enemy knight - If your knight level is higher than an opponent’s you can displace the enemy knight so the opponent must relocate it or remove it. Both knights need to be connected to each other by roads.
section6.chasingRobber: Chasing away the Robber - You can move the Robber if it is on a tile that one of your active knights is touching. You may do this with multiple knights in the turn, as long as they were active before your turn started.

section7.title: 7. Barbarians vs. Knights
section7.whenBarbariansAttack: When the Barbarian Ship reaches the end of the tracker, they attack.
section7.calculateBarbarianStrength: Barbarian strength = total number of Cities
section7.calculateKnightStrength: Strength of Knights = total strength of all Active Knights
section7.ifStrengthIsEqual: If Knight strength is equal or greater to Barbarian strength:
section7.defenderOfColonist: Player with most active Knights is awarded with Defender of Colonist, worth 1 extra Point.
section7.defenderOfColonistDraw: If players are tied for the highest Knight strength, each of those players will choose a Progress Card instead.
section7.barbariansWin: If Knight strength is less than Barbarian strength:
section7.playersLoseConsequence: Player with lowest Knight strength gets their city destroyed, turning it into a settlement.
section7.playersLoseWithNoCities: Players with no cities, as well as players whose cities are all Metropolises, are not affected.
section7.afterAnAttack: After an attack, barbarians return to the start of the track and all knights are deactivated.
section7.playerDestroyCityNote: Players who must destroy one of their cities, but already have 5 settlements on the board, must first rebuild that destroyed city before building any other cities.

section8.title: 8. No early Robber
section8.noEarlyRobber: Players CANNOT move the {{- robberIcon}} Robber until the first barbarian attack but players must still discard if they have over 7 cards (this includes using your knight to move the Robber, as well as using a Bishop Progress Card).

section9.title: 9. City Walls
section9.cityWallsDescription: City Walls increase your discard limit by 2 cards, helping to protect you from losing cards when a 7 is rolled.
section9.maximumCityWalls: Each player can place a maximum of 3 walls, reaching a maximum of 13 cards discard limit.
section9.oneCityWallPerCity: A city can only have 1 wall.
section9.cityDestroyed: If a city is destroyed by the barbarians, the wall on that city is destroyed as well.

section10.title: 10. City Improvements
section10.differentCommodities: 3 different types of City Improvements can be bought with commodities.
section10.youMustHaveOneCity: You must have at least 1 city to buy City Improvements.
section10.cityImprovementsAffectProgressCards: City Improvements affect what Progress Cards you receive based on red dice.
section10.cityImprovementCostIncrease: Each City Improvement level requires more commodities to buy.
section10.cityImprovementCostDescription: Each level of City Improvement costs one more resource.
section10.level3Unlocks: Upgrading a City Improvement to level 3 unlocks a special ability
section10.tradingHouse:
Trade (Trading House)
Trade commodities at a 2:1 rate for any other resource or commodity
section10.aqueduct:
Science (Aqueduct)
If none of your numbers roll, or if your number is blocked, you get to select a resource of your choice from the bank (unless a 7 rolls).

section11.title: 11. Metropolis
section11.metropolisDescription: The first player to reach level 4 in a City Improvement type, can upgrade a city to a Metropolis, worth 2 Points
section11.oneMetropolis: Only 1 Metropolis for each City Improvement type.
section11.playersCanStealMetropolis: Players can steal a Metropolis if they reach level 5 City Improvement first.
section11.playersCanHaveMoreThanOneMetropolis: Players can have more than 1 Metropolis.
section11.playersMustHaveAnAvailableCity: Players must have an available city to buy a level 4 City Improvement. You cannot upgrade to a Metropolis or purchase a level 4 City Improvement without an available city.

section12.title: 12. Progress Cards
section12.progressCardsReplaceDevelopmentCards:
In Cities & Knights, Progress Cards replace Development Cards.
There are 18 of each type of Progress Card.
section12.collectProgressCards: Collect Progress Cards based on event dice + red dice + City Improvement level.
section12.handLimit: You can only have 4 Progress Cards in your hand. However, you may have 5 on your own turn. If you end your turn with 5 Progress Cards, you must immediately discard 1 of them.
section12.5thCardDiscard: If you draw a 5th Progress Card when it’s not your turn, you must discard 1 Progress Card from your hand.
section12.victoryPointsDiscard: Points from Progress Cards (Printer & Constitution) do not count towards the 4 cards in your hand.

section13.title: 13. Science Progress Cards
section13.alchemistDescription: Play at the beginning of your turn before the dice roll. Determine the roll of the red and regular dice
section13.craneDescription: Build a City Improvement for one commodity less. These cannot be combined together to pay for 2+ less commodities in one turn
section13.engineerDescription: Build a City Wall for free if you have a city
section13.irrigationDescription: Collect 2 Grain cards for each individual Grain tile you have a settlement or city on
section13.medicineDescription: Upgrade a settlement to a city for 2 Ore cards and 1 Grain
section13.miningDescription: Collect 2 Ore cards for each individual Ore tile you have a settlement or city on
section13.smithDescription: Upgrade up to 2 knights for free

section14.title: 14. Trade Progress Cards
section14.commericalHarborDescription: Force each player to trade you a commodity of their choice for one of your resources. You may finish using this card early without doing all available trades
section14.masterMerchantDescription: Choose 1 player that has more points than you to see their resource and commodity cards. Choose 2 cards to steal from their hand
section14.merchantFleetDescription: Pick 1 resource or commodity. You may trade it at a 2:1 rate for any other resource or commodity until the end of your turn
section14.merchantDescription: Move the Merchant to any tile touching one of your settlements. You can do 2:1 trades with this resource as long as it stays there. Having control of this Merchant gives you 1 point.
section14.resourceMonopolyDescription: Select a resource for all players to give you 2 of
section14.tradeMonopolyDescription: Select any commodity for all players to give you 1 of

section15.title: 15. Politics Progress Cards
section15.bishopDescription: Move the Robber and steal 1 card from each player on the tile the Robber is moved to
section15.deserterDescription: Choose an opponent to remove a knight of their choice. You may place one of your knights for free if you have an available spot
section15.diplomatDescription: Remove any open road. If it is your own road, you may relocate it.
section15.intrigueDescription: Displace an enemy knight touching one of your roads. If there is no available space for the opponent to place it, it must be removed from the board
section15.saboteurDescription: All players that have equal or more points than you must discard half of their resource/commodity cards.
section15.spyDescription: Select a player to see all their Progress Cards and steal 1 of them
section15.warlordDescription: Activate all of your knights for free
section15.weddingDescription: All players with more points than you will give you 2 resources or commodities of their choice

section16.title: 16. Points to win
section16.firstPersonTo13VP: The first person to get to 13 points is the winner.
section16.winOnYourTurn: In order to win, you have to reach 13 points on your turn. You may still lose if another player achieves 13 points on their turn even if you had 13 points before them. Note: points to win may vary while combining Cities & Knights and Seafarers expansions, depending on maps and scenarios.
section16.getPointsDoingTheFollowing: Get points by doing the following:
section16.highestKnightStrength: Highest Knight strength when defeating the Barbarians (Defender of Colonist)
section16.progressCardVP: Earn a Progress Card that provides one Point (Printer & Constitution)

section17.title: 17. FAQ
section17.Q1: ● I received my 13th Point with a Progress Card (or Defender of Colonist) on someone else's turn. Why didn’t I automatically win?
section17.A1: You can only win the game on your own turn. So you only win if you still have 13 points when your regular turn starts.
section17.Q2: ● Am I allowed to pick commodities from a city on a gold tile?
section17.A2: No, you are only allowed to pick resources from gold tiles, even with cities.
